import pandas as pd

from lets_plot import *
LetsPlot.setup_html(offline=True)

Comic mode — every renderer-migrated geom¶

Set theme(comic=True) to render a plot in xkcd-style hand-drawn mode.

Data — Palmer penguins¶

In [2]:
import numpy as np

# penguins.csv sits next to this notebook — fully offline, no network/SSL.
penguins = pd.read_csv('penguins.csv').dropna().sort_values('bill_length_mm')

# Per-species summary, for the interval geoms (errorbar / linerange / pointrange / crossbar / lollipop).
summ = penguins.groupby('species', as_index=False).agg(m=('body_mass_g', 'mean'), s=('body_mass_g', 'std'))
summ['ymin'] = summ['m'] - summ['s']
summ['ymax'] = summ['m'] + summ['s']

# Flipper length vs bill length, binned, to get a band + ordered path for the path/ribbon family.
# (computed on a throwaway frame so no Interval column lands on penguins itself)
_bins = pd.cut(penguins['bill_length_mm'], bins=20)
band = (penguins.groupby(_bins, observed=True)
        .agg(x=('bill_length_mm', 'mean'), m=('flipper_length_mm', 'mean'), s=('flipper_length_mm', 'std'))
        .reset_index(drop=True).dropna())
band['ymin'] = band['m'] - band['s']
band['ymax'] = band['m'] + band['s']
band['g'] = (band['x'] < band['x'].median()).map({True: 'shorter bills', False: 'longer bills'})

Lines & paths — drawPath / drawArrowhead¶

In [3]:
# geom_path — connects points in data order
ggplot(band, aes('x', 'm')) + \
    geom_path(size=1) + \
    facet_wrap('g', scales='free_x') + \
    ggtitle('geom_path') + \
    theme(comic=True)

# geom_segment — straight segments, here with arrowheads

                    'xend': [1, 2, 3], 'yend': [2, 1, 3], 'g': ['A', 'A', 'B']})
ggplot(seg) + \
    geom_segment(aes('x', 'y', xend='xend', yend='yend'), arrow=arrow(), size=1) + \
    facet_wrap('g') + \
    ggtitle('geom_segment') + \
    theme(comic=True)

In [8]:
# geom_spoke — segments defined by angle + radius
import numpy as np
grid = pd.DataFrame([(x, y) for x in range(5) for y in range(5)], columns=['x', 'y'])
grid['angle'] = np.arctan2(grid['y'] - 2, grid['x'] - 2)
ggplot(grid, aes('x', 'y')) + \
    geom_spoke(aes(angle='angle'), radius=0.6, arrow=arrow(), size=0.8) + \
    ggtitle('geom_spoke') + \
    theme(comic=True)
Out[8]:
In [9]:
# geom_abline / geom_hline / geom_vline — reference lines all wobble
ggplot(penguins, aes('bill_length_mm', 'body_mass_g')) + \
    geom_point(color='gray') + \
    geom_hline(yintercept=4200, color='#d73027', size=1) + \
    geom_vline(xintercept=45, color='#1a9850', size=1) + \
    geom_abline(slope=100, intercept=-200, color='#4575b4', size=1) + \
    ggtitle('geom_hline / geom_vline / geom_abline') + \
    theme(comic=True)

Composite & annotation geoms¶

In [33]:
# geom_bracket — bracket lines wobble; the label rides the comic font
bracket_df = pd.DataFrame({'xmin': ['Adelie'], 'xmax': ['Gentoo'], 'y': [6500], 'label': ['p < 0.05']})
ggplot(penguins, aes('species', 'body_mass_g')) + \
    geom_boxplot(aes(fill='species'), alpha=0.3) + \
    geom_bracket(aes(xmin='xmin', xmax='xmax', y='y', label='label'), data=bracket_df) + \
    ggtitle('geom_bracket') + \
    theme(comic=True)
Out[33]:
In [34]:
# geom_text_repel — leader lines wobble; the text rides the comic font
labels = penguins.drop_duplicates('species')
ggplot(penguins, aes('bill_length_mm', 'flipper_length_mm')) + \
    geom_point(color='gray') + \
    geom_text_repel(aes(label='species'), data=labels, size=7, seed=42) + \
    ggtitle('geom_text_repel') + \
    theme(comic=True)
